info.title: pressbox
info.description: The HTTP API of pressboxd, the pressbox server. A token belongs to one user, and every answer is about that user's feeds and state. Timestamps are Unix seconds (UTC). Responses are compressed (gzip or brotli) when the request's `Accept-Encoding` allows it. Breaking changes will go to a new version (`/api/v2/`), served alongside `v1` for a while. See docs/api.md for more.

post.summary: Marks every item in a feed read.

200.description: `updated` counts the items that were unread

404.description: No such feed, or not this user's

get.summary:
A page of items, newest first. To get the next page, pass the previous
page's `next_cursor` as `cursor` with the same filters.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Full-text search over titles and text. Words are matched as prefixes
and all must appear.

parameters.name: media
parameters.description: `true`: only items with media; `false`: only items without.

parameters.name: in_progress
parameters.description:
`true`: only unread items with a saved playback position, i.e.
started and not finished.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Skips this many items. Slow deep into a long list; prefer `cursor`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Starts after the item a previous page's `next_cursor` names. Opaque;
takes precedence over `offset`.

400.description: A malformed cursor, or a search over 16 words or 500 characters

post.summary:
Marks read every item a list shows, however many pages it has, or with
`from` only that item and the older ones after it.

200.description: `updated` counts the items that were unread

400.description: A search over 16 words or 500 characters

404.description: No such item, or not this user's

get.summary:
The episode's chapters, read from its chapters file. Files are fetched
once and kept for a week.

404.description: No such item, or it has no chapters

502.description: The chapters file couldn't be fetched or read

put.summary: Saves where the user stopped playing an episode. The last write wins.

404.description: No such item, or not this user's

put.summary: Marks an item read or unread. Marking it read takes it out of Up Next.

404.description: No such item, or not this user's
No such item, or not this user's

get.summary:
The episode's best transcript (one in the show's language before a
translation, then JSON, WebVTT, SRT, HTML and plain text), as timed
segments. Files are fetched once and kept for a week.

404.description: No such item, or it has no transcript

502.description: The transcript couldn't be fetched or read

delete.summary:
Revokes the device whose token made the request, as when a client
signs out. The static token isn't a device: it is removed from the
configuration instead.

400.description: The static token is not a device

get.summary: This document, the API's OpenAPI description.

post.summary:
Asks to pair a device. Show the `code` to the user, who approves it on
another device or with `pressboxctl`, then poll with `poll_id`.

get.summary: Whether a pairing was approved. The token is given once.

delete.summary:
Denies a pairing. Only admins may, so one user can't turn away another's
new devices.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code shown on the device, e.g. `K7-4QX`

post.summary: Approves a pairing, for the approver's user or, for admins, another one.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code shown on the device, e.g. `K7-4QX`

403.description: Only admins can approve for other users

put.summary: Replaces the Up Next queue with `ids`, in order.

post.summary:
Fetches every feed now, except those fetched within the last minute (ten
minutes for a feed whose last fetch failed).

get.summary:
What the server is. Public, so a client can check what it talks to
before pairing.
For load balancers and service managers.

ApproveRequest.description:
Optional body for approving a pairing. Only admins may name another
user; by default the device goes to the approver's user.

user.description: The user it was added to.

hidden.description: Only changes the artwork: leave it out of a chapter list.

image.description: Artwork to show during the chapter.

url.description: A web page about the chapter.

Chapters.description:
Response to `GET /api/v1/items/{id}/chapters`, from the episode's
Podcasting 2.0 chapters file.

bitrate.description: Bits per second, if the feed says.

height.description: Video height in pixels, if the feed says.

length.description: Size in bytes, if the feed says.

title.description: A label for choosing between enclosures, e.g. `"1080p"`.

ErrorResponse.description:
The body of every error response (4xx and 5xx), e.g.
`{"error": "not found"}`.

error.description: What went wrong, in English, for showing to the user.

Feed.description: A feed declared in the server configuration, with its current state.

archived.description:
The feed was removed from the configuration but is kept because it
has starred items. It is no longer fetched.

episodes.description:
How many of `total` are podcast episodes (items with media), so
clients can tell podcasts from news. Absent from servers before
26.0.

id.description: The attribute name used in the Nix configuration, e.g. `"lwn"`.

image.description: The feed's artwork (`itunes:image`, the RSS `<image>`, Atom's logo).

last_error.description: The error from the last fetch, if it failed.

last_fetched.description: When the feed was last fetched, successfully or not.

site_url.description: The website the feed belongs to, if it says.

title.description: The configured title, or the title the feed reports about itself.

content.description:
Full HTML content, if the feed provides it. Only included by
`GET /api/v1/items/{id}`; list responses leave it out.

oneOf.description: Audio or video attached to the item (a podcast episode), if any.

position.description:
Where this user stopped playing the media, in seconds; 0 if they
haven't started it (or finished it).

published.description: Publication time, or the time pressbox first saw the item.

summary.description: Short HTML summary, if the feed provides one.

ItemPage.description: A page of items, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page; `None` on the last page.

next_offset.description:
Pass as `offset` to get the next page; `None` on the last page, and
when paging by `cursor`. Kept for older clients; prefer `next_cursor`.

cursor.description:
Starts after the item a previous page's `next_cursor` names. Opaque;
takes precedence over `offset`.

in_progress.description:
`true`: only unread items with a saved playback position, i.e.
started and not finished.

media.description: `true`: only items with media; `false`: only items without.

offset.description: Skips this many items. Slow deep into a long list; prefer `cursor`.

q.description:
Full-text search over titles and text. Words are matched as prefixes
and all must appear.

allOf.description:
The list's filters, as for `GET /api/v1/items`. `limit`, `offset`
and `cursor` are ignored.

from.description:
Only this item and the ones after it in the list (older ones), if
set. Nothing is marked if the user can't see this item.

MarkRead.description:
Body of `POST /api/v1/items/read-all`: marks the items a list shows as
read, in one request however many pages the list has.

Me.description: Response to `GET /api/v1/me`: who this token belongs to.

device.description: The device's name, or `None` for the static token.

Media.description:
An item's audio or video, from RSS `<enclosure>`, Atom `rel="enclosure"`
links and JSON Feed attachments, with the iTunes and Podcasting 2.0
(`podcast:`) tags that describe it.

chapters.description:
The `podcast:chapters` file. Clients use `GET
/api/v1/items/{id}/chapters`, which reads it for them.

duration.description: Length in seconds, if the feed says.

enclosures.description:
The files: the feed's own enclosure first, then any
`podcast:alternateEnclosure`s (other formats, bitrates or video) in
the order the feed lists them. Never empty.

image.description: The episode's artwork, if it has its own.

transcripts.description:
The `podcast:transcript` files. Clients use `GET
/api/v1/items/{id}/transcript`, which reads the best one for them.

PairApproved.description: Response to `GET /api/v1/pair/{poll_id}` once approved. Returned only once.

name.description: The name it was registered under (made unique if needed).

PairPending.description:
Response to `GET /api/v1/pair/{poll_id}` (202) while the request waits
for approval.

PairRequest.description: Body for `POST /api/v1/pair`: a client asking to be paired.

name.description: A name for the device, e.g. `"laptop"`. Shown when approving.

code.description: Short code to approve, e.g. `"K7-4QX"`. Show it to the user.

poll_id.description: Secret to poll `GET /api/v1/pair/{poll_id}` with. Keep it private.

PendingPairing.description: A pairing request waiting for approval.

position.description:
Seconds into the media. 0 forgets the position (when the media was
finished, say).

Queue.description:
Response to `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/queue`: the user's Up Next list, the
episodes to play next in order. Items come as in lists, without `content`.

QueueOrder.description:
Body for `PUT /api/v1/queue`: the whole list in order, replacing the one
before. Clients add, remove and reorder by sending the list they want.
Items the user can't see, items without media, and repeats are left out.

start.description: Seconds from the start; 0 for untimed (HTML or plain) transcripts.

Transcript.description:
Response to `GET /api/v1/items/{id}/transcript`: the episode's best
transcript (JSON, WebVTT, SRT or HTML), as timed segments. Very short
cues (some files time every word) are joined into sentences.

token.description: A paired device's token, or the static `tokenFile` token
